sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Bartow County, Georgia?
sections.html:
The Bartow County Tax Commissioner bills and collects the tax, and the Board of Tax Assessors sets the value it is based on. The tax office sits in the Frank Moore Administration and Judicial Building at 135 W. Cherokee Avenue, Suite 217A, in Cartersville, and takes property tax calls at (770) 387-5111, Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., holidays excluded.

Bartow is a sole commissioner county, which means one elected commissioner adopts the budget and the millage rates instead of a multi-member board. Cartersville is the seat and the largest city. Adairsville, Euharlee and Kingston have their own governments, and Cassville, Rydal and Allatoona are unincorporated communities. A sale of a house in any of them runs through the same county tax office for the county and school bill, so the steps below apply countywide.

  • Tax office: bills, payments, mobile home taxes, excess funds claims after a tax sale.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: values, returns, homestead questions and appeal notices.
  • County Commissioner: adopts the annual millage rates at a public meeting each summer.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Bartow County before listing?
sections.html:
Bartow County is in the northwest part of Georgia and now counts as part of the Atlanta metro area, mainly around Cartersville, which is more than 40 miles up I-75 from downtown Atlanta. The county covers about 459 square miles of land, and Lake Allatoona, the Etowah River and Red Top Mountain State Park shape the southeastern side. Main roads include US 41, US 411, SR 20, SR 61, SR 113, SR 140 and SR 293.

Growth is the story for sellers. The Census Bureau counted 108,901 residents in 2020 and estimates 120,800 for July 2025, about 11 percent more in five years. Children attend either the Bartow County School District or Cartersville City Schools, so a Cartersville address and a county address do not feed the same schools. The county commissioner's August 2026 minutes describe a large industrial tax base, a battery plant and data center development as reasons the county can keep lowering its rates.

sections.h2: When are Bartow County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bartow County bills once a year, with bills mailed on or about September 15 and payment due November 15. The 2026 bills followed that pattern, with a November 15, 2026 due date. Mobile home bills run on a separate calendar and are due April 1.

The county bills the owner of record on January 1. A buyer who takes title later in the year should call the tax office and ask for a duplicate bill, because the original goes to the January 1 owner. The county site also warns that not receiving a bill does not excuse a missed due date.

  • Pay online through the link on the Tax Commissioner page, in person, by phone, or by mail to the office address above.
  • Card payments online, in person or by phone carry a 2.5% convenience fee, according to the county billing page.
  • Checks go to the Bartow County Tax Commissioner, 135 W. Cherokee Ave., Suite 217A, Cartersville, GA 30120.

The state Department of Revenue notes that interest does not begin until 60 days after the postmark date of the bill, and that unpaid balances can also pick up penalties. Ask the tax office for the current interest figure, since it changes with the state rules.

sections.h2: What millage rates did Bartow County set for 2026?
sections.html:
The county adopted 7.11 mills for incorporated areas and 6.76 mills for unincorporated areas in August 2026, down from 7.40 and 6.87. The minutes say the commissioner used the rollback rate, which changed the total digest by only about 1 to 4 percent, and that rates have fallen steadily since 2013.

A mill is one dollar of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, and Georgia assesses property at 40 percent of fair market value. Bartow also has a school levy, so the figure on your own bill will include more than the county rate. Your bill is the number that counts, and the tax office can tell you the school rate for your district.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption work in Bartow County?
sections.html:
The exemption lowers the assessed value of your primary residence, and the county deadline to file is April 1. The county billing page adds that it covers a primary home only, so rentals, multi-family units and commercial or industrial property do not qualify.

The August 2026 commissioner minutes describe the standard exemption as $15,000 and say the county was working with state lawmakers to raise it to $30,000 in a later year. Treat that as a plan the county voiced, and ask the Tax Commissioner what amount applies to your bill. Someone who sells and buys another Bartow home must apply again for the new address, and the state says failing to apply counts as waiving the exemption.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Bartow County assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked within 45 days of the date the assessment notice was mailed. The state Department of Revenue sets that rule for every county, and it covers disagreements about fair market value on the notice.

A taxpayer can also file a return between January 1 and April 1, which proposes a value before the board sets one. A refund claim for tax that was assessed or collected in error must start within three years of payment, and a refund from a successful appeal is processed automatically once the final value is set. A lower value helps a seller twice: it reduces the bill and gives a buyer a lower number to carry.

  • Keep the notice and its mailing date.
  • Gather recent sales of similar homes in your part of Bartow.
  • Photograph defects that the assessor may not know about.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell a Bartow County house?
sections.html:
The unpaid tax stays with the property, so the bill has to be settled at or before closing. The county bills the January 1 owner, which means a seller who owned the home on that date usually receives the bill even if the sale closes before November 15. Ask the closing office to confirm who pays the year's tax and how it is divided.

If taxes go unpaid and the county sells the property at a tax sale for more than what is owed, the extra money is held as excess funds. The Tax Commissioner page links an excess funds claim form. For a house with back taxes, a quick sale often means paying the county first from the proceeds, so request a payoff figure from the tax office before you agree to a closing date. A buyer who purchases as is should ask for the same figure.

faqs.q: What date are Bartow County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The 2026 bills were due November 15, 2026, and Bartow bills on that November schedule each year, with bills mailed around September 15. Mobile home bills are due April 1.

faqs.q: What is the Bartow County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 is the deadline to apply, per the Tax Commissioner page. The exemption applies only to your primary residence, so a rental or second home does not qualify.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Bartow County property value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice, and the written appeal must be postmarked by then and sent to the Board of Tax Assessors.

faqs.q: Does the Tax Commissioner mail the bill to my mortgage company?
faqs.a: The county bills the owner of record on January 1, so check with your lender about whether it pays from escrow. If you bought during the year, call the tax office at (770) 387-5111 and ask for a duplicate bill in your name.

faqs.q: Can I pay Bartow County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, by card online, in person or by phone, with a 2.5% convenience fee on every debit or credit card payment. Checks by mail avoid that fee.
